problems: stop 1 card 2, answer 3: copies a Prep line word for word

explanations.explanation: That’s exactly what Paul says: ‘Stand firm, then, and do not be encumbered once more by a yoke of slavery.’ Friend, freedom in Christ isn’t a suggestion—it’s a stance.

explanations.answer: Work hard to earn their freedom
explanations.explanation: Paul says Christ already set them free. Working to earn it would be like trying to bake a cookie that’s already done—you’d just burn the dough.
Paul doesn’t whisper freedom—he shouts it! ‘It is for freedom that Christ has set us free.’ Keeping quiet would be like hiding a cookie right out in the open.
Yep. Paul warns them not to be weighed down again by a yoke of slavery. That’s a heavy mixing bowl on their backs, and Paul’s telling them to set it down.
Nope. Paul says the opposite: don’t be encumbered again by slavery. He’s not mincing words here—he’s handing them a shovel to dig out from under that yoke.
Paul puts it plain: ‘Christ will be of no value to you at all.’ Friend, that’s like trying to bake with salt instead of sugar—you won’t get what you’re after.
Paul doesn’t say that. He says Christ becomes worthless to them if they go down that road. It’s not a boost—it’s a bust.
Nope. Paul says Christ’s value drops to zero if they add circumcision as a requirement. It’s not ‘same’—it’s ‘gone.’
Paul says the exact opposite: a man who gets circumcised is obligated to obey the whole law. That’s not just one command—it’s the whole recipe book.
Right. Paul says they’re on the hook for the whole law, not just circumcision. It’s like trying to follow one rule in a kitchen where every burner’s lit—you can’t do it.

explanations.answer: They have been severed from Christ
explanations.explanation: Paul doesn’t sugarcoat it: ‘You who are trying to be justified by the law have been severed from Christ.’ Friend, that’s a clean break, not a close call.

explanations.answer: They have drawn closer to Christ
explanations.explanation: No way. Paul says they’ve fallen away from grace. Trying to earn it with the law pushes them away, not closer.
Paul says the opposite: they’ve lost grace, not gained it. It’s not about earning more—it’s about trusting what Christ already did.
Paul says it plain: ‘by faith we eagerly await through the Spirit the hope of righteousness.’ Friend, faith is the oven that bakes this hope golden-brown.
Paul says the law won’t get them there. It’s like trying to bake with a recipe that’s already burnt—it won’t rise.
Effort alone won’t cut it. Paul says faith is what matters. It’s not about how hard you knead—it’s about trusting the dough will rise.
Paul says it’s not about the outward mark—it’s about faith working through love. Friend, that’s the kind of cookie that smells like heaven.
Paul says outward rules don’t matter. It’s not about perfect obedience—it’s about a heart that loves because it’s been set free.

explanations.answer: Coming from the right family line
explanations.explanation: Paul says family lines don’t cut it. It’s not about who your ancestors were—it’s about who your Savior is.
Paul says the persuasion slowing them down doesn’t come from God. It’s like someone whispering ‘add more salt’ when the recipe already calls for sugar—it’s not from the One who calls them.
Right. Paul says it doesn’t come from the One who calls them. It’s a counterfeit voice in the kitchen, and Paul’s calling it out.
Paul says a little leaven works through the whole dough. Friend, that’s like a single rogue chocolate chip spreading its flavor everywhere—it changes the whole batch.
Nope. Paul says it works through the whole batch. It’s not just a surface issue—it’s a full-kitchen takeover.
Paul says it spreads everywhere. It’s not a local problem—it’s a global one in the dough.
Paul says the one troubling them will bear the judgment. Friend, that’s not a light warning—it’s a gavel coming down.

explanations.answer: He will be let off free
explanations.explanation: Paul doesn’t say that. He says the troubler will face judgment. It’s not a free pass—it’s a reckoning.

explanations.answer: He will be put in charge
explanations.explanation: No way. Paul says the troubler will answer for it. It’s not a promotion—it’s a penalty.
Paul says he’s NOT still preaching circumcision. He’s asking why he’s persecuted if he were—which means he’s not.
Right. Paul isn’t admitting he preaches circumcision. He’s pointing out the absurdity of the charge by turning it back on them.
Paul says don’t use your freedom as an opportunity for the flesh. Friend, freedom isn’t a license to make a mess in the kitchen—it’s a chance to serve others.
Nope. Paul says the opposite: don’t use freedom for the flesh. It’s not a free-for-all—it’s a call to love.
Paul says the whole law is fulfilled in this one command. Friend, that’s the golden rule—simple, but it covers every burner in the kitchen.
Paul doesn’t mention the Sabbath here. It’s not the command he’s pointing to—it’s the command to love.
Paul doesn’t cite this command. It’s not the one that sums up the law in this moment—it’s love.
Paul warns that biting and devouring one another leads to being consumed. Friend, that’s like a kitchen fire spreading until there’s nothing left but ashes.
Paul says they’ll be consumed, not scattered. It’s not a gentle breeze—it’s a wildfire.
Paul doesn’t say that. He says they’ll be consumed. It’s not about shame—it’s about destruction.
